## Standard

<a id="BoxDrawing"></a>

### Box drawing

`BoxDrawing` · `src/text.ts:47`

The characters of the Unicode Standard that draw lines across the cells of a monospace grid: Trame draws the branches of a tree and the steps of a path with them.

Source: The Unicode Standard, Version 15.1, code chart Box Drawing (U+2500 to U+257F) · `https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/U2500.pdf`

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `vertical` | `│` | U+2502 BOX DRAWINGS LIGHT VERTICAL: a line that goes on below |
| `verticalAndRight` | `├` | U+251C BOX DRAWINGS LIGHT VERTICAL AND RIGHT: a branch, with others below it |
| `upAndRight` | `└` | U+2514 BOX DRAWINGS LIGHT UP AND RIGHT: the last branch, or a step under the one before |

- Maintained by: trame
- Used by: [Path step](#PathStep), [Tree branch](#TreeBranch)

### Tree branch

`TreeBranch` · `src/text.ts:171` · status: **held**

A branch of a tree, under its parent: the lines already drawn on its left, a corner (the last branch) or a tee (a branch with others below it), the name of the link, then the node it leads to. ## Decisions

<a id="TerminalColumns"></a>

### Columns in the terminal

`TerminalColumns` · `src/text.ts:37`

The terminal shows tables as columns of text: each column as wide as its widest cell, then a gap. Lines written one at a time (a report as it goes, the issues of a list, the layers of the graph) do not know their widest cell: their columns have a fixed width, the rank of a layer, the severity and the source of an issue, the name of a kind or of a view. A text too wide for its column still keeps the smallest gap before the next one.

| Case | Value |
|---|---|
| gap | 2 |
| minimumGap | 1 |
| widths | { rank: 9, severity: 15, source: 22, name: 14 } |

- Decided by: trame
- Used by: [Preparation](commands.md#Preparation), [Publish](commands.md#Publish), [Test the laws](commands.md#TestKinds), [Plain text writer](rendering.md#PlainTextSyntax), [Figures as text](rendering.md#TextFigures), [Columns](#Columns), [Padded cell](#PaddedCell)

<a id="TerminalText"></a>

### Terminal text

`TerminalText` · `src/text.ts:20`

What Trame shows in a terminal is plain text in lines, read in a monospace font: no markup, no colour, no control sequence. Position shows the structure: what belongs to something is indented under it, one step per level; columns are aligned with spaces; trees and paths are drawn with box-drawing characters. Several blank lines in a row make one, and the text ends with an end of line. Each construct declares its own marks in its syntax element; the marks they share are here: the space that aligns, the step of indentation, the blank lines allowed in a row.

| Case | Value |
|---|---|
| space |   |
| indent |    |
| maxBlankLines | 1 |

- Decided by: trame
- Rejected: Markdown, a terminal does not render it: its marks would be read as they are; Colours and control sequences, an output is not always a terminal (a file, a pipe, a test): the text must say everything without them, and it is compared line by line from one generation to the next; Tabs, their width depends on the terminal: columns would no longer line up
- Used by: [Advance](commands.md#Advance), [Amend](commands.md#Amend), [Assembler](commands.md#Assembler), [Audit the packages](commands.md#Audit), [Plan](commands.md#Plan), [Preparation](commands.md#Preparation), [Publish](commands.md#Publish), [Test the laws](commands.md#TestKinds), [Plain text writer](rendering.md#PlainTextSyntax), [Code lines](#CodeLines), [Columns](#Columns), [Item line](#ItemLine), [Padded cell](#PaddedCell), [Path step](#PathStep), [Lines of the terminal](#TerminalLines), [Tree branch](#TreeBranch)
